17 An object slides with constant velocity across a horizontal sheet of ice. Friction is negligible.
A constant horizontal force of 2.1 N is then applied to the object as shown.
X
4.0 m
2.1 N
30
object
initial direction of
motion of object
A short time after applying the force, the object reaches point X at a displacement of 4.0 m from
its position when the force was first applied.
What is the work done by the force on the object as it travels to point X?
A
4.2 J
B
4.8 J
C
7.3 J
D
8.4 J

hints: Notice the $4.0 \text{ m}$ displacement to point X is at $30^{\circ}$ to the $2.1 \text{ N}$ horizontal force, not in the same direction.
Recall work done by a constant force depends on the component of displacement along the force: $W = Fs\cos\theta$ where $\theta$ is the angle between them.
First calculate the displacement along the force as $4.0\cos 30^{\circ}$, then multiply by $2.1 \text{ N}$ to get work in joules.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: force $F = 2.1 \text{ N}$ to the right, displacement magnitude $s = 4.0 \text{ m}$ to X, and angle between them $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ from the diagram.
State the rule for work done by a constant force at an angle to displacement: $W = Fs\cos\theta$. Only the component of displacement in the direction of the force does work.
Resolve the displacement along the force direction: $s_{\parallel} = s\cos\theta = 4.0 \times \cos 30^{\circ}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $2.1 \times 4.0 = 8.4$ and $8.4 \times 0.8660 = 7.27 \text{ J}$, which is about $7.3 \text{ J}$ with correct joule unit for $\text{N m}$.

A.explanation: This is $2.1 \times 4.0 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 4.2 \text{ J}$. It uses the component perpendicular to the force instead of the component along the force.

B.explanation: This value does not follow from $W = Fs\cos\theta$ with $F = 2.1 \text{ N}$, $s = 4.0 \text{ m}$ and $\theta = 30^{\circ}$. It uses an incorrect resolved component.

C.explanation: This is $2.1 \times 4.0 \times \cos 30^{\circ} = 7.3 \text{ J}$, the component of the $4.0 \text{ m}$ displacement along the $2.1 \text{ N}$ force.

D.explanation: This is $2.1 \times 4.0 = 8.4 \text{ J}$. It ignores the $30^{\circ}$ angle between the force and the displacement to X.
